newsitem.title: USA: U.S. to seek waiver of immunity for Ukrainian.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to seek waiver of immunity for Ukrainian.

text.p: The United States said on Monday it would ask the Ukraine to waive diplomatic immunity for the wife of a Ukrainian diplomat charged with causing a three-car collision after drinking alcohol.

State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said the case of Olesy Yarotskiy, wife of second secretary Vadym Yarotskiy, was the fourth drunken driving incident involving a diplomat from the former Soviet Union in the Washington area this year.
"We're going to ask the Ukrainian government for a waiver of diplomatic immunity. And if it is granted she ... will appear in court for prosecution," he told reporters.
"And if a waiver is not granted, then her driving privileges will be suspended for a year," he said. He stressed that diplomats were not above the law and should not be.

Yarotskiy, 45, was charged with driving while intoxicated after she failed a breathalyzer test following the collision late on Saturday, when her car struck a second car, pushing it into the car ahead of it. No one was injured.

Burns said the State Department was also seeking a waiver of immunity for two other diplomats, one from Kyrgyzstan and one from Russia, who were involved in separate alleged drunken driving accidents.

The most serious case this year was that of Georgian diplomat Gueorgui Makharadze, whose immunity was waived by his government after he was involved in a car crash that killed a teenage girl in Washington in January. Makharadze pleaded innocent to charges of involuntary manslaughter and aggravated assault and was scheduled to be tried starting on July 21.
